passage: I am Madhuri, and my father is Gurpreet. When I finally told Papa about the boys who hid my shoes every day, his face went dark. "I am going to the school right now," he said, reaching for his keys. I panicked. I had wanted him to hear me, not to shout at people in the corridor. "Papa, please sit," I said. He stared, then sat, and I saw his hands shaking. "Thank you for telling me, beta," he said. "Tell me everything." I talked for a long time. The next morning we went together to meet the principal, and Papa let me speak first. I felt safe, and glad I had told him.

qa.q: What had the boys done to Madhuri every day?
qa.a: They hid Madhuri's shoes every day.

qa.q: Why did Madhuri panic when her father reached for his keys?
qa.a: Madhuri wanted him to listen, not go and shout at people at the school, and feared he would take over.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet do next that helped, and why?
qa.a: He sat down, thanked Madhuri for telling him and listened to everything, then went with Madhuri to the principal and let Madhuri speak first, which made Madhuri feel safe.

qa.q: What might Gurpreet have been feeling as he sat down with shaking hands?
qa.a: He was probably angry and frightened for Madhuri, but he held it back so that he could listen.

grounding: A child confesses bullying to a father who first wants to storm in, then listens, thanks the child and plans with the school.

passage:
Tuesday. Gurpreet finally told Papa about the boy who kept tearing her notebooks. Harish went red and grabbed the car keys. "I'll go to that school right now!" Gurpreet grabbed his arm. "Please, Papa, don't! Everyone will know!"
Harish stopped. He sat back down. "You're right. Tell me everything first." He listened, then said, "Thank you for trusting me."
Wednesday. They made a list together of dates and torn pages. Harish emailed the class teacher and asked for a meeting with Gurpreet present.
The next Monday. The boy had been moved to another section. That evening Gurpreet told Papa about a small fight with her friend, without being asked.

qa.q: What was the boy doing to Gurpreet's notebooks?
Why did Gurpreet grab Papa's arm?
qa.a: She was panicked and embarrassed that everyone would know if he stormed into school.

qa.q: What did Harish do that made telling feel safe?
qa.a: He stopped, listened first, thanked her, and made a plan with her and the school instead of storming in.

qa.q: How might Harish have felt when he first heard about the notebooks?
qa.a: He likely felt angry and protective, wanting to rush to the school to stop it at once.

grounding: A father wants to storm into school after his daughter confesses bullying; he stops, listens, thanks her and plans with the school, and she keeps telling him things.

passage:
"Pooja, did I ever tell you how your Neelam Dadi learned to speak up? When I was ten, a girl pulled my plait every day and called me names. I told my brother first. He said, 'Stop being so sensitive.' So I kept quiet for months.
Then one night I cried at dinner, and it all came out. My father stood up, face like thunder. 'I'll go to that school and shout at her father!'
My mother put a hand on his arm. 'Sit. Let her finish.' He sat. He listened to every word, then said, 'Thank you for telling us.' The next morning we went together, calmly, to see the headmistress."

qa.q: What did the girl at school do to young Neelam every day?
qa.a: She pulled her plait and called her names.

qa.q: Why did young Neelam keep quiet for months?
qa.a: She felt dismissed and ashamed after her brother told her to stop being so sensitive, so she decided not to tell anyone.

qa.q: What turning point in the story helped young Neelam most?
qa.a: When her mother made her father sit and listen before acting, so he thanked her and they went calmly to the headmistress together.

qa.q: How did young Neelam's father first react to her story?
qa.a: He was angry and protective, standing up and threatening to go and shout at the girl's father.

grounding: A grandmother recalls being told to stop being so sensitive, which silenced her, and how her father, urged to listen first, thanked her and planned with the school.
